headline: Internal: uniform framework access across the library
summary: An internal consistency refactor with no API or behavior change. Every library module now captures the framework once at the top (`var b = require("./index").framework;`) and uses `b.*` uniformly, replacing a per-module lazy accessor and its scattered call sites. Two source files that embedded a raw NUL byte as a map-key separator now use the `\u0000` escape, so the whole library is plain text. New lint rules lock both in place. Public APIs, runtime behavior, and the published surface are unchanged.

items.title: Framework handle captured once per module
items.body: Library modules previously reached the vendored framework through a lazy `_b()` accessor invoked at every call site. They now capture it once at module top — `var b = require("./index").framework;` — and reference `b.*` directly, matching how the edge worker already accesses it. This is safe because the entry point exposes `framework` before its require cascade. No public API or runtime behavior changes.

items.title: Lint detectors for accessor uniformity and source hygiene
items.body: Two repository lint rules now prevent drift: one rejects the reintroduction of the per-module lazy framework accessor (use the top-level capture), and one rejects raw C0 control bytes in source files (write `\u0000` and friends as escapes so files stay plain text — grep / diff / editors handle them correctly).
